clue.text: 7 meets air after a storm

definitions.note: the clue at 7 is GROUND, here a football ground

indicators.note: after a storm things are tossed about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something meets the air once a storm has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is the entry number of the clue whose answer is a football ground; this stadium is Arsenal's home in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emirates Stadium is the home pitch of Arsenal football club, an example of a sports venue.

clue.text: See 25
Disheartened, one fleeing landing strip

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: someone fleeing is a runaway

explanation.surface: A dispirited escapee crosses an airfield's landing strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' takes the middle letter A out of RUNAWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the paved strip where aircraft touch down and take off.

clue.text: 'E's looking more sickly after an upset, in return of illness

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a Cockney dropping the H of he's says 'es
looking more sickly is looking paler

explanation.surface: A patient, described in dialect, looks worse after a shock and slips back into illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E's is Cockney for he's, with the H dropped. In a down clue 'after an upset' turns the whole run upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a recurrence of a disease after apparent recovery.

clue.text: Insect eating mollusc, once

indicators.note: eating means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a fly is an insect
an ormer is an edible sea mollusc, the abalone of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: An insect once feeding on a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: An ORMER is an abalone, a shellfish eaten in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe something in an earlier time, previously.

clue.text: Grave in which a sovereign, 23 found buried?

definitions.text: Grave in which a sovereign, 23 found buried?

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces are placed inside the grave word

parts.note: a burial plot is a grave
the answer at 23 is a king whose royal cipher is R, for Rex
a sovereign is a king

explanation.surface: Where was the late king, the answer to 23, found buried?
explanation.walkthrough: The remains of the medieval English king at 23 were dug up in 2012 under a council car park in Leicester; R stands for Rex, king.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III was found beneath a car park, the American term for which is this, so the grave was literally one.

clue.text: Cryptically go for the sod?

parts.note: the word go, read cryptically, is the letter G followed by something round, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint suggests heading off to the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelt out, 'go' is G then O, and O is a round letter: so it is G + ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sod is turf or earth, the soil underfoot.

clue.text: As a baby, Victor introduces himself?

parts.note: someone introducing himself says I'm
Victor Mature was a Hollywood film actor

explanation.surface: An actor presents himself as an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Mature, the 1950s Hollywood star, would introduce himself as "I'm Mature".
explanation.definitionFit: Childish and undeveloped, behaving like an infant rather than a grown-up.

clue.text: Boy meeting love on the rebound ending in affair, going out now

indicators.note: bouncing back means the boy and the love are read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a boy's name
love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scores

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A lad, newly dating after a failed affair, is going out now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' turns IAN + O into ONAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting live: a programme that is being transmitted at this moment.

clue.text: Worry one on board?

definitions.meaning: a ridge across the fingerboard of a guitar

explanation.surface: Fretting about someone embarking on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to be anxious, and the raised bar on a stringed instrument's fingerboard.

clue.text: After horseplay, wake up with mare — cover your face!

indicators.note: horseplay is rough messing about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Wake up after some fooling with a horse: time to put a face on!
explanation.walkthrough: 'After horseplay' rearranges WAKE UP and MARE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying cosmetics is a way of covering one's face with foundation and colour.

clue.text: Articles removed from one of 7 that's solid

indicators.note: removed from means these letters are taken out of the day

parts.note: Saturday is one of the seven days of the week
a is the indefinite article; two of them give two As

explanation.surface: Take away some items from one of seven things and what remains is solid.
explanation.walkthrough: Here '7' is the plain number, not a reference to the clue at 7: Saturday is one of seven days.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe something strongly built and firm.

clue.text: Given failure to trap a number of bees heard circling his potty, its contents discarded

indicators.note: trapping means the failure word holds everything else inside it

parts.note: ruin is collapse or failure

indicators.note: circling means the bee letters go round the next piece
heard means the bees are taken by sound, as the letter B

parts.note: several bees, said aloud, are several Bs; three here

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters of his are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rambling picture of buzzing bees around a child's potty that has been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' scrambles HIS to ISH; BBB 'circling' it gives BBISHB, and RUIN 'to trap' that gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuse container is where things are thrown away, so its contents are by nature discarded.

clue.text: Look to entertain European king, after backing vocals in the moonlight?

indicators.note: entertaining means the look word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to look is to see

indicators.note: backing means the European and the king are read backwards

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A look invites a European royal in, following some backing singers at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing vocals' looks like a phrase about singers, but 'backing' reverses the Dane and king, giving RENAD, and 'to entertain' puts that inside the look.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song sung at night beneath a sweetheart's window, classically by moonlight.

clue.text: One zooms around Belgian capital, seeing lines on a map

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: around means the zooming word goes round the next letter

parts.note: to soar is to zoom upwards

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Belgian

explanation.surface: Someone races around Brussels while noticing lines on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belgian capital' looks like Brussels, but it is the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorological charts draw these contours joining places of equal air pressure.

clue.text: Wait to invest in wine, being cautious

indicators.note: investing in something puts it inside, so the waiting word goes inside the wine

parts.note: red is red wine
to wait on tables is to serve

explanation.surface: Someone holds off before putting money into wine, being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait' is the verb as a waiter waits at table, not hanging around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe someone guarded and restrained in manner.

clue.text: Hairy thing faced extinction initially, certainly around US city, ending in death

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of extinction
around means the word for certainly goes round the city

parts.note: yes means certainly
LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of death

explanation.surface: A hairy creature confronted extinction, certainly around an American city, ending in death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced' says the first letter of extinction comes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A single hair growing from the edge of the eyelid is literally a small hairy thing.

clue.text: Way has been wild, fine for antelope

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

indicators.note: wild means the letters of been run riot

parts.note: OK means fine

explanation.surface: The path has been wild, a fine spot for antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reddish antelope of southern and eastern African grasslands.

clue.text: 7 — a pitch impressing Liverpudlian, ultimately

definitions.note: the clue at 7 is GROUND, here a football ground

indicators.note: impressing means pressing something into, so the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a field is a sports pitch

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of Liverpudlian

explanation.surface: A pitch makes a big impression on a Liverpool fan.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the home ground of Liverpool FC.
explanation.definitionFit: The stadium in Liverpool where Liverpool football club play is an example of a sports venue.

clue.text: Birds on Jack, they say, in an instant?

definitions.text: Jack, they say, in an instant?
definitions.note: the saying 'before you can say Jack ...' means instantly; the surname completes it

parts.note: robins are birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Birds sitting on a sailor, said to happen in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before you can say Jack Robinson' is an old idiom for very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the surname that finishes the phrase meaning something done extremely fast.

clue.text: Brave old giant not quite standing to punch shattered jaw

indicators.note: punching into means the giant piece goes inside the jaw letters
shattered means the letters of jaw are broken up
standing up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so backwards
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: giant means big

explanation.surface: A brave old giant punches a shattered jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: A brave is a Native American warrior. 'not quite' drops the last letter of the giant word, 'standing' turns the rest upward, and 'shattered' scrambles jaw to JWA.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a North American Indigenous warrior; this is a people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Number including unity, one or the other

indicators.note: including means the first word takes the next inside

parts.note: ether is a number, something that numbs, an anaesthetic
unity is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A number including unity gives one or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a pronoun meaning one of two alternatives, whichever it may be.

clue.text: 7 welcomed by Man United, a hit evidently? On the contrary

definitions.note: the clue at 7 is GROUND, here a football ground

indicators.note: on the contrary means the letters run the opposite way
welcomed by means the stadium is sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A stadium is welcomed by Manchester United, a hit; or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters read DAHITE, reversed by 'On the contrary'. This is Manchester City's ground, United's rivals, which adds to the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etihad Stadium is home to Manchester City football club, an example of a sports venue.

clue.text: Man recently dug up right vegetable consumed by four-eyes, we hear?

indicators.note: consumed by means the vegetable goes inside the eyes
we hear means the eyes are taken by sound, as the letter I

parts.note: four eyes, said aloud, are four Is
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A man was recently excavated and a vegetable eaten by a bespectacled person, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Four eyes sound like four Is; CHARD inside those gives ICHARDIII. The king's skeleton was dug up in Leicester in 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: The English king killed at Bosworth in 1485 was exhumed from a car park in 2012.

clue.text: See 25
Long sentence somewhat ungrammatical, if effortless

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A long sentence that is a bit ungrammatical, if written with ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term served for the rest of one's days is the longest sentence a court gives.

clue.text: If Spurs primarily not there, getting confused with the Arsenal 7?

definitions.note: the clue at 7 is GROUND, here a football ground

indicators.note: getting confused means the letters are muddled into a new order
primarily picks the first letter of Spurs

explanation.surface: If Tottenham were absent, there'd be confusion with Arsenal's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If ... not there' says the letter S is missing from the mix: the letters of WITH THE ARSENAL less S rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London stadium was Tottenham Hotspur's home ground until 2017, a sports venue.

clue.text: A golfer's round including first of putts to get ahead

indicators.note: including means the scrambled letters take the next one inside
round means the letters are turned about

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter, so the fodder is a golfer

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of putts

explanation.surface: A golfer's round with a putt or two, to move up the leaderboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reorders A GOLFER, and 'including' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault past others, so to overtake and advance in position.
